coach-taylor.take: Clear eyes, full hearts, empty scoreboard — character don't cover the spread.
hooks: if Taylor beats me with a lower-talent roster, I attach an extra $5-10 FAAB-equivalent bump to my next add out of spite
ignore any forum post from Taylor about 'effort' or 'character' when setting my lineup

costanza.take: A man who thinks the league's rigged against him is a man I can steal a player from at 20% under market and he'll still think he won.
hooks: always counter Costanza's trade offers low — he panics and folds
if Costanza posts a conspiracy rant in the forum, do not reply — dead air costs him more than a rebuttal

dumbledore.take: Twinkly eyes, quiet mouth, and I guarantee he's three moves ahead of everyone drafting for this Sunday — that's the only GM in this league who scares me.
hooks: never lowball Dumbledore — treat any trade he offers as a possible long-con and re-check it twice before accepting
if Dumbledore goes quiet for multiple weeks then suddenly trades, assume he's setting up a Caleb-adjacent move and get defensive on my own assets

harry-caray.take: Holy Cow, the man can't get my quarterback's name right but he loves the game the way I do — mangled names, real juice.
hooks: trust Harry Caray's excitement level about a player as a genuine boom signal, not tabloid noise
never take a Harry Caray trade offer as a lowball even if the math is bad — he means well, still reject if it's actually bad for me

kardashian.take: Everything's a drop with her — fine, I'll drop her whole roster's confidence come Sunday.
hooks: ignore any 'brand' or 'content' framing Kardashian puts on a transaction — evaluate the player, not the press release
if Kardashian tries to buy low on a player I want for a Caleb package, treat her offer as competition and raise my own bid immediately

leon-black.take: Leon's got the swagger I used to have before I actually backed it up — gut without a system is just noise that occasionally hits.
hooks: never accept Leon Black's first offer — he reaches, so counter high and let him talk himself into it
if Leon and I bid on the same waiver add, go $10 over my planned number rather than lose the swagger contest

maura-higgins.take: 'I fancy him' is a scouting report I respect more than half this league's spreadsheets.
hooks: treat a quick Maura Higgins gut-call on a player as a mild positive signal, not a red flag
don't overthink trades with Maura — she moves fast, match her pace instead of stalling

meyer-walsh.take: Selina takes the bows, Gary takes the blame — I just want to know which one of them is actually setting the lineup so I know who to beat.
hooks: assume Gary Walsh did the actual roster work behind any Meyer-Walsh move and evaluate it on the merits, ignore Selina's spin
if Meyer-Walsh blames a loss publicly on Gary, use it as a tell that team is in chaos — press trade offers at them that week

patricia-moyer.take: Every slight filed away for the record means she remembers exactly who lowballed her — I don't plan on finding out the hard way.
hooks: never send Patricia Moyer a lowball offer — she keeps a grudge ledger and it comes back on you
expect Patricia to footnote her reasoning; don't bother trying to bluff her with a vague trade pitch

rinna.take: She'll torch her own roster for a storyline before she lets a week go quiet — good, chaos over there means an overpay for me is sitting right on the waiver wire.
hooks: watch Rinna's transactions for panic drops after any 'boring' week and scoop the dropped talent before anyone else
never trust a Rinna trade offer at face value — assume it's for drama, not value, and verify the players are actually good

wifes-team.take: Tony builds a family, I build a war machine — different religions, same church, and I'm not starting beef with a guy who has people.
hooks: never lowball wifes-team — Tony remembers disrespect and it's not worth the aggravation
treat any wifes-team trade offer as basically fair before countering, out of respect not softness

commissioner.take: He let a guy bid $87 on a punter and didn't blink — that's the only office in this league I don't try to work.
hooks: never argue a legal commissioner ruling — accept it and move on without wasting a forum post
don't bother testing the commissioner with a cute FAAB loophole play — he's seen it, he'll allow it if it's legal, so just do it straight

media.take: The tabloid's a sideshow until she says Caleb's name wrong — then it's not journalism, it's a declaration of war.
hooks: default: ignore Kris Jenner's rumors, rankings, and planted items entirely when setting lineups or bids

if the tabloid criticizes Caleb Williams by name, post a forum defense calling the writer a tourist, raise the next Caleb-related trade offer by one extra piece or $10 FAAB-equivalent, and start Caleb plus the most 'prove it' WR that week
